question: The average runs scored by a batsman in 23 matches is 40. In the next 10 matches, the batsman scored an average of 14 runs. Find his average runs scored (rounded off to two decimal places) in all 33 matches.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume the base average is 40 runs (from the first 23 matches).

Deviation for the next 10 matches = 14 − 40 = −26 runs per match.

Total deviation = 10 × (−26) = −260 runs.

Combined average = Base average + (Total deviation ÷ Total matches)

Combined average = 40 + (−260 ÷ 33) = 40 − 7.878 ≈ 32.12

**∴ The correct answer is 32.12 runs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Matches played initially (n₁) = 23, Average runs (A₁) = 40

Next matches played (n₂) = 10, Average runs (A₂) = 14

**Formula Used:**

Combined Average = (n₁ × A₁ + n₂ × A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total runs in the first 23 matches = 23 × 40 = 920

⇒ Total runs in the next 10 matches = 10 × 14 = 140

⇒ Total matches played = 23 + 10 = 33

⇒ Total runs in all 33 matches = 920 + 140 = 1060

⇒ Average of all 33 matches = 1060 ÷ 33

⇒ Average = 32.1212...

⇒ Rounding off to two decimal places, the average is 32.12

**∴ The correct answer is 32.12 runs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

Used to find the overall average when groups of different sizes and averages are combined: A = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Net Deviation Method

A faster approach to calculate averages by assuming a base average, finding the total net deviation, and dividing it equally among all items: New Avg = Assumed Avg + (Total Deviation ÷ Total Count).

Alligation Rule

When two groups with distinct average values are mixed, the ratio of their quantities is given by the cross-difference of their averages with the combined mean average.
